title: C2S-Scale: a model-generated cancer hypothesis confirmed in cells
summary: The 27-billion-parameter single-cell model, built on Gemma with Yale, predicted that silmitasertib would increase antigen presentation only in an immune-positive context. In human neuroendocrine cell models with low-dose interferon, the increase was about 50%. Validation is in cells only; the authors call this ‘a first step.’

evidence.tested: The model's prediction that silmitasertib boosts antigen presentation with low-dose interferon was tested experimentally in human neuroendocrine cell models not seen in training, with a roughly 50% synergistic increase reported.
evidence.unknown: The article calls this an early first step, validation is in cell models only, and clinical use is not shown.
evidence.ai_role: The 27B single-cell language model C2S-Scale ran a dual-context virtual screen of over 4,000 drugs and generated the hypothesis.
